issues.detail: The skill is tightly tied to Intercom and Next.js/React with Node-specific server code, and mobile (iOS/Android) setup is mentioned in the compatibility field but never covered in the instructions.

The two examples are prose descriptions of a request and a result with no runnable code or concrete output, and the second one only sketches the Stripe webhook handler and the PUT /contacts/{id} call.

scenarios.name: nextjs-secure-messenger-logged-in
scenarios.rationale: A matches nearly every rubric item: the SDK in a client component, an HS256 JWT signed with INTERCOM_MESSENGER_SECRET that includes user_id, the JWT sent without user_hash, shutdown() in the cleanup, and enforcement of identity verification. B uses the deprecated HMAC user_hash and no JWT, and it has no intercom_user_jwt or HS256 signing. B does include the SDK, shutdown(), and enforcement, so it earns partial credit.

scenarios.name: sync-upgrade-to-intercom-contact
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric item (env-var Bearer token, Intercom-Version header, custom_attributes plan 'pro', POST /messages inapp from admin 394051 to the contact id, a client trackEvent, and both the data-attribute and 404-retry caveats), while B has most of the server pieces and the data-attribute setup but fires the client event through window.Intercom('trackEvent') instead of the SDK's trackEvent, doesn't mention the 404 retry, and leaves Maria's lookup as placeholders.

scenarios.name: eu-workspace-logout-and-spa-navigation
scenarios.rationale: Both configure the EU api_base with app_id, call update() on route changes, and call shutdown() on logout; A explicitly keeps the identity secret server-side but never frames app_id as the only public value, while B's server-side JWT signing with INTERCOM_MESSENGER_SECRET and its public-app_id comment cover the secrets rubric point a bit more directly, and B also adds the EU REST endpoint note.
